before.title: 3.6L High Feature V6 (LY7) Timing Chain Stretch
before.description: The 3.6L 'High Feature' V6 used in the redesigned 2008-2010 Vue (and shared with Aura/Outlook/Acadia/CTS) is prone to timing chain stretch, often aggravated by extended oil-change intervals. As the chains and plastic guides wear, cam/crank timing drifts out of correlation, triggering the check-engine light, rough running, and a rattle on cold start. GM issued Information Bulletin 12-06-01-009F covering timing chain kit and guide replacement for DTCs P0008/P0009/P0016/P0017/P0018/P0019.
before.solution: Verify oil level and condition first; severely stretched chains require replacing the timing chains, tensioners, and guides as a complete set (often all three chains on this engine). Owners can reduce risk by using the correct dexos1-spec oil and changing it at conservative (e.g., ~5,000-mile) intervals rather than relying on the oil-life monitor's longer recommendations.
symptoms: Check engine light
Rattle or rattling on cold start
Rough idle / engine running rough
Reduced power
Timing correlation fault codes

proposal.title: 3.6L High Feature V6 (LY7) Timing Chain Stretch
proposal.description: GM bulletin 12-06-01-009 directly includes 2008-2010 Saturn VUE vehicles with the 3.6L LY7 and addresses worn or stretched timing chains associated with P0008, P0009 and P0016-P0019. It supplies the applicable chain kit and an Oil Life Monitor calibration check, but does not establish that every LY7 is prone to failure, a mileage-based recurrence, cold-start rattle as the defining test or extended oil intervals as the sole cause. Crucially, GM says idler sprockets, camshaft actuators, the crankshaft gear and chain guides must not be replaced automatically; guides are replaced only when their wear block reaches the base friction material.
proposal.solution: Check oil level, condition and service history, scan all codes and freeze-frame data, and follow the LY7 cam/crank-correlation diagnosis before opening the timing drive. If chain wear is confirmed, use the VIN/build-specific GM procedure and chain kit, inspect rather than automatically replace guides and gears, and verify whether the Oil Life Monitor calibration update applies. Do not buy a timing-chain kit, guides, sprockets, actuators or an engine from this page; VIN, LY7 verification, DTC diagnosis, measured wear and calibration history determine the repair, with no universal retail part.

P0016-P0019 after factory correlation diagnosis
Oil level or condition requiring correction before timing diagnosis
Measured chain or guide wear confirmed during the specified procedure

before.title: Front Subframe / Lateral Link Corrosion in Salt-Belt Regions
before.description: Owners in northern, road-salt states report premature corrosion of the front subframe/cradle and rear lateral (suspension) links on early Vues, with cases of the subframe rusting through and causing unstable steering. GM acknowledged related rear lateral-link issues, and rear wheel/lateral link concerns were addressed under earlier recall activity. Severe corrosion can make the vehicle unsafe to drive and is expensive to repair on an older vehicle.
before.solution: Have the subframe, control arms, and rear lateral links inspected for structural rust, especially before purchase in salt-belt areas; corroded structural members must be replaced. Regular undercarriage washing and rust-inhibitor treatment can slow further corrosion on otherwise sound vehicles.
symptoms: Visible structural rust on subframe/cradle
Corroded rear lateral links
Unstable or wandering steering
Clunking over bumps
Failed safety/structural inspection

before.title: Ignition Key Can Be Removed When Not in 'Off' — Rollaway Recall (14V490)
before.description: On affected 2002-2004 Vue vehicles, the ignition lock cylinder can wear such that the key may be removed when the ignition is not in the 'Off' position. Owners can verify open recalls by VIN on the NHTSA website and have the remedy performed free at any GM dealer.

before.title: Power Steering Line Nut Loosening — Leak and Fire Recall (08V470)
before.description: On 2008-2009 Vue models, the nut securing the power steering line to the power steering pump can loosen, allowing high-pressure power steering fluid to leak. The fluid can contact hot exhaust components and potentially cause an engine-compartment fire. GM recalled 42,408 vehicles under NHTSA campaign 08V470000. Many owners separately reported sudden loss of power steering assist with no warning, and some VINs were not included in the recall population.
before.solution: Under the recall, dealers inspect the power steering line nut; if no leak is present they tighten it, and if a leak is found they tighten the nut and top off/verify the fluid. Owners experiencing ongoing leaks or loss of assist outside the recall should have the pump, lines, and rack-and-pinion seals inspected for the leak source.
symptoms: Power steering fluid leak
Low or empty power steering reservoir
Sudden loss of power steering assist
Heavy or hard steering

before.title: V6 Valve Cover Gasket Oil Leak Soaking Coil Boots → Misfires
before.description: On the 3.0L and 3.5L V6 Vue models, the valve cover gaskets become brittle and leak oil down into the spark plug tubes. The oil soaks the coil-on-plug boots, causing the rubber to swell and degrade so spark grounds out, producing misfires and rough running. Oil also drips onto the exhaust manifold, creating a burning-oil smell.
before.solution: Replace the leaking valve cover gaskets and clean oil from the spark plug tubes, then replace the oil-soaked coil boots (and plugs if fouled). Replacing only the boots without fixing the valve cover gasket leak leads to repeat failure, so address the gasket as the root cause.
symptoms: Engine misfire
Rough idle / poor performance
Burning oil smell
Oil in spark plug tubes
Check engine light (misfire codes)

proposal.title: V6 Valve Cover Gasket Oil Leak Soaking Coil Boots → Misfires
proposal.description: The frozen 2004-2007 population uses the 3.5L V6, not the 3.0L V6 also asserted in the live text. Factory material provides separate left/right rocker-cover gasket service, oil-leak diagnosis and P0300-P0306 diagnostic paths, but no exact bulletin found establishes brittle cover gaskets as a recurring cross-year defect that routinely fills plug tubes, destroys boots and causes misfires. A 2004 VUE bulletin also shows that P0300-P0306 can accompany PCM-terminal faults, demonstrating why the codes do not prove a gasket-to-boot mechanism.

If oil is actually present in a plug well, inspect the exact cover seal, spark plug, boot and coil and then diagnose each stored misfire using the 3.5L chart, including ignition, fuel, compression, wiring and PCM-terminal checks as applicable. Keep oil off hot exhaust parts and address active smoke safely. Do not buy cover gaskets, coil boots, coils or spark plugs from this page; confirmed leak location, cylinder evidence and electrical/mechanical test results determine the repair, with no universal retail part.

before.title: VTi (VT25-E) Continuously Variable Transmission Failure
before.description: The 4-cylinder Vue's VTi CVT was GM's first high-volume CVT and proved badly unreliable, with the steel push-belt and related components wearing out prematurely. Owners experienced slipping, shuddering, jerky/erratic shifting, loud whining on acceleration, and sudden power loss, with many units failing entirely between 50,000 and 100,000 miles. GM halted VTi production in January 2004 and later settled a class-action lawsuit covering more than 90,000 Saturn Vue and Ion vehicles. This is the single most-reported Vue problem on owner-complaint databases.
before.solution: There was no durable repair; failed units were replaced with rebuilt/replacement transmissions costing roughly $3,500-$5,000. GM extended the powertrain warranty on VTi units to 5 years/75,000 miles and provided reimbursement under the class-action settlement. Many owners with later failures opted to replace the vehicle rather than the transmission given its high cost relative to resale value.
symptoms: Transmission slipping
Shuddering during acceleration
Jerky or erratic shifting
Loud whining noise on acceleration
Sudden loss of power

before.title: Vue VTi CVT Catastrophic Failure (2002-2005)
before.description: Early Saturn Vue (2002-2005) was offered with the GM VT25 (VTi) continuously-variable transmission paired with the 2.2L Ecotec. The CVT was infamously unreliable — failure rates so high that GM extended warranty to 5 years/75,000 miles, and many independents won't touch them. Symptoms: belt slip noise, surge under acceleration, eventual no-drive.
before.solution: If still under the extended warranty, get it documented. If out of warranty, the practical options are: (1) used VTi CVT swap (~$1,200-$2,500 with risky reliability), (2) used 5-speed manual conversion ($1,500-$3,000 with parts hunt), or (3) part out / sell the vehicle. Aamco / GM dealers historically offered swap-with-Aisin-5-speed conversions but parts are hard to source.
symptoms: CVT slip noise
surge under acceleration
shuddering
no drive
limp mode

proposal.title: Vue VTi CVT Catastrophic Failure (2002-2005)
proposal.description: Saturn bulletin 04020B and the VT25E diagnostic bulletin support concerns only on 2002-2005 VUE vehicles equipped with VTi RPO M16/M75. The frozen engine entry identifies the 2.2L application, but the frozen V6 trim is incompatible with the VTi population and the page duplicates the other published VTi failure identity. The exact sources do not support calling every failure catastrophic, the live price ranges, independent-shop refusal, manual-conversion path or claimed Aisin conversion offering. The historical five-year/75,000-mile policy is also expired for these model years and must not be presented as current coverage.
proposal.solution: Verify the VIN, 2.2L engine and M16/M75 transmission RPO, then diagnose the exact no-movement, hesitation, noise or DTC condition under the applicable VT25E procedure. Treat the V6-tagged indexed scope as unresolved and do not infer VTi fitment from this page. Do not buy a used VTi, sensor, belt, case cover, manual-swap package or replacement vehicle from this page; RPO, DTCs, pressure data, internal findings and current VIN-specific support determine the next step, with no universal retail part.
symptoms: Verified M16/M75 VTi loses Drive or Reverse
P0841, P1758 or P1882 after factory diagnosis
Launch hesitation or noise reproduced under the applicable procedure
V6-tagged vehicle fails the VTi fitment gate
affectedSystems: VT25E/VTi RPO M16 or M75 only
Pressure, sensor, case-cover, belt/sheave and clutch paths
